C-01.1.answer: Absence still refuses before anything is read: an input that is not a TTY, or a TTY without setRawMode, gets UI_PASSWORD_NEEDS_TTY. After the fix setRawMode(true) is the first thing promptHidden does, so if turning echo off throws, the promise rejects before a prompt is shown or a key is read; nothing is read as success.
C-01.1.guard: test/console-login.test.mjs::sakk ui refuses a password on the command line and a password prompt without a terminal

C-01.2.answer: The new test records every setRawMode call and every prompt write in one order log. Moving setRawMode(true) back below output.write(prompt) turns it red; I run it on the unfixed promptHidden first and keep the red in the commit message, so the order is a required check, not an optional one.
C-01.2.guard: test/console-login.test.mjs::the hidden prompt turns echo off before it shows the prompt (F-240)

C-04.1.answer: The bound does not change: promptHidden keeps at most 1024 characters of one line and refuses a non-terminal input before reading; the fix only swaps the order of two calls and adds no loop or wait. The bound is declared in the cost-bounds table for promptHidden and checked by a counter-style test, not a stopwatch.
C-04.1.guard: test/cost-bounds.test.mjs::every exported function shows how its work is bounded

C-05.1.answer: The sentence 'asks for it and does not echo it' (UI_PASSWORD_NEEDS_TTY hint, both tutorials) was false in the 0.4.0 tutorial run: the second password showed in the transcript. The new test backs it by asserting echo is off before each prompt appears. The CHANGELOG entry says only that, and names the limit the test does not cover: keys typed before a prompt appears are echoed by the terminal itself.
C-05.1.guard: test/console-login.test.mjs::the hidden prompt turns echo off before it shows the prompt (F-240)

C-05.2.answer: No figure or exit code changes. UI_PASSWORD_NEEDS_TTY, UI_PASSWORD_MISMATCH and UI_PASSWORD_CANCELLED keep their text and exit 2, and the hint they print still names a command that works: sakk ui --set-password at a terminal.
C-05.2.guard: test/claims-are-checked.test.mjs::every code the user-facing docs name exists in the code

C-09.1.answer: The code assumed a person reads the prompt and then types, slower than the switch to raw mode. Under expect, a pty driver that answers the moment it reads the prompt, the second password was echoed: libuv applies the mode only after earlier output has drained, so the prompt is visible before echo is off. I tried that environment after the fix: the same expect step, repeated, shows no password.
C-09.1.guard: test/console-login.test.mjs::the hidden prompt turns echo off before it shows the prompt (F-240)

C-09.2.answer: It runs as sakk ui --set-password at an operator's terminal, with process.stdin as the TTY and stderr for prompts, from bin/sakk.mjs through askConsoleLogin. I show it there by running the repository's bin under expect in a throwaway HOME, the way the tutorial run did, not only through the fake stream in the unit test.
C-09.2.guard: test/console-login.test.mjs::the hidden prompt turns echo off before it shows the prompt (F-240)

C-10.1.answer: Turning echo off before the prompt was a habit, not a check. It is now an assertion in npm test, which the gate, the pre-push hook and CI all run, so a change that shows the prompt first fails before it can merge.
C-10.1.guard: test/console-login.test.mjs::the hidden prompt turns echo off before it shows the prompt (F-240)

C-10.2.answer: There is no other route: grep finds setRawMode only in promptHidden, both password prompts in askConsoleLogin call promptHidden, and bin/sakk.mjs reaches it only through askConsoleLogin. The username line is meant to be visible and uses readline.
C-10.2.guard: test/console-login.test.mjs::the hidden prompt turns echo off before it shows the prompt (F-240)
